solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Created from a rib, she is anticipating a Fall

indicators.note: something created from other material is built by reworking it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eve, made from Adam's rib, is waiting to fall from grace in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eden picture makes 'Created from a rib, she' look like a description of Eve, but 'Created from' is the anagram signal working on A RIB plus SHE. The capital F on 'Fall' misdirects towards the Fall of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: On the stock market a bear expects prices to drop, so a bearish trader is one who foresees a fall.

clue.text: Package containing very loud sound regulator

indicators.note: the package word holds the loudness marking inside it

parts.note: a bale is a bound package of goods such as hay
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A parcel holding a noisy device to control sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A baffle is a panel or partition that controls or deadens the passage of sound, as in a loudspeaker.

clue.text: Value actor's lead on stage

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it
lead means the first letter of the word actor's is used

parts.note: to mount a play is to stage it

explanation.surface: An actor's worth as a leading performer in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount of something is its total worth or sum, which is its value.

clue.text: Cayman cousin giving his all for this month's fomenter

indicators.note: the reptile gives up its letters A, L, L in exchange for the abbreviation for this month's

parts.note: a cayman is a crocodilian, a close relative of the alligator
INST, instant, is the old commercial abbreviation for this month's

explanation.surface: A reptile relative working flat out for the troublemaker of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his all' points literally at the letters ALL; 'inst.' as in 'your letter of the 5th inst.' is old business-letter style.
explanation.definitionFit: A fomenter stirs up trouble, and an instigator is one who provokes or incites such action.

clue.text: Very hard to grasp follower of GMT's tiny accommodation

indicators.note: the very-hard letters grasp, hold, the time standard between them

parts.note: HH marks a very hard pencil lead
UTC, Coordinated Universal Time, succeeded GMT as the world's time standard

explanation.surface: A cramped room that is hard to find for someone keeping to Greenwich time.
explanation.definitionFit: A hutch is a small cage housing rabbits, so it is cramped lodging for a pet.

clue.text: Remains in vehicle, departs by avenue

indicators.note: the departs-and-avenue pieces sit in the vehicle, so they go inside its word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: A grim scene: a body found in a car that drives off down an avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: Remains are a dead body, and a corpse kept for dissection or study is the same thing.

clue.text: Sauce available in two types of saloon area

parts.note: a saloon is a car, and also a bar

indicators.note: available goes in the two saloon words

parts.note: a saloon is a bar as well as a car
on means available, as in the dish is on today

explanation.surface: A sauce served in a couple of kinds of saloon bar.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives two pieces: a saloon is both a car and a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonara is an Italian pasta sauce of egg, cheese and bacon.

clue.text: Old man swallowing tablet becomes numb

indicators.note: the old man word swallows the tablet, taking it inside

parts.note: your old man is your father, your dad
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A father takes a pill and loses all feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb that has gone dead has lost sensation, so it is without feeling.

clue.text: Wandering clean through by way of Mediterranean area

indicators.note: the scrambled word passes through the middle of the route word

parts.note: via means by way of

indicators.note: wandering means the letters of the next word stray from their order

explanation.surface: Roaming cleanly across a Mediterranean region.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a Spanish city and region on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Singer's last great single, covering trendy music hated in cinema?

indicators.note: the other pieces cover, surround, the trendy word
last means only the final letter of the word Singer's is taken

parts.note: GT is the abbreviation for great, as in Gt Britain
one means single
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A singer's final hit, fashionable but loathed by filmgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile phone's ring tone going off during a film is the tune audiences hate to hear.

clue.text: Down following bereavement

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in 'p. 5f'
a bereavement is the loss of someone close

explanation.surface: Someone feeling down after a death in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' reads as low spirits, but it is the soft fluffy material.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is soft fluffy fibre, and silky floss from plants or silk cocoons is that kind of fluff.

clue.text: Waterproof headgear: Biedermann, say, is seen with one in pool

indicators.note: Biedermann and one are placed in the pool, so they go inside its word

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain pool
Paul Biedermann is a German champion swimmer, an example of someone called Paul
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A swimmer seen in a pool wearing a waterproof cap.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimming picture suggests the pool is a swimming pool; here it is a mountain tarn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin was a sailor's hat made of tarred, waterproofed cloth.

clue.text: Peculiar speech that's landed hospital in it with palace site

indicators.note: the landed-and-hospital pieces go in 'it', the peculiar speech just named

parts.note: lingo is jargon or a language peculiar to a group
lit, as a bird lit on a branch, means landed
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: An odd dialect that has brought a hospital into a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Linlithgow is a Scottish town whose palace was the birthplace of Mary, Queen of Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Linlithgow Palace, a ruined royal residence in West Lothian, stands in the town of that name.

clue.text: Tension in belly and even parts of skin and mouth

indicators.note: the second and fourth letters of each word, the even-numbered positions, are kept

explanation.surface: Nervous tension felt in the stomach, the skin and the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight sensation of nerves in the stomach is described as a knot in the belly.

clue.text: Words of Candle in the Wind, perhaps a line to eulogise more

parts.words: Words of Candle in the Wind, perhaps
parts.note: a candle is made of wax, and the words of a song are its lyric, so the words of a candle are its wax lyric

explanation.surface: Elton John's tribute song quoted to praise someone even more.
explanation.walkthrough: Candle in the Wind is Elton John's song, reworked as a tribute to Princess Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax is to grow, so to wax lyrical is to become ever more effusive in praise.

clue.text: Raver in speech to endorse a foreigner

indicators.note: in speech says the phrase is to be heard, not read, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to endorse is to back, and a foreigner is an alien: back an alien

explanation.surface: A partygoer's slurred speech in favour of supporting an immigrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunken reveller at a wild party is a bacchanalian, after the riotous rites of Bacchus, god of wine.

clue.text: Therapy that's exuberant, suppressing nothing and admitting overdose

indicators.note: the word then admits, lets in, the overdose abbreviation
the exuberant word holds down nothing inside itself

parts.note: chirpy means lively and cheerful
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A lively therapy that holds back nothing but allows an overdose.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiropody is the treatment of foot ailments, a form of medical therapy.

clue.text: Laughing stock snared by factual disproof

indicators.note: the laughing stock is caught inside the factual word

parts.note: real means factual, true
a butt is the target of jokes

explanation.surface: A figure of fun caught out by a factual counterargument.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is an argument that refutes a claim, so it is a refutation.

clue.text: Pension manager maybe more faithful with limits of taxable incoming

indicators.note: the outer letters of taxable come into the more-faithful word

parts.note: holier means more devout, more faithful

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pension fund manager who is more honest about taxable income.
explanation.walkthrough: A pension here is a French-style boarding house, not a retirement fund.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension is a small guest house on the Continent, and one who runs a guest house is an innkeeper.

clue.text: Chill with old record in laid-back request: party's ending without dissipation

indicators.note: laid back means reclining, so that combination is laid the other way and read from right to left
the old record goes in the chill word

parts.note: ice is a chill, as in ice in someone's voice
a mono recording is an old single-channel record
a call is a request, as in a call for help

indicators.note: ending means the final letter of the word party's is taken

explanation.surface: Relaxing with an old album at a mellow party, nothing wasteful going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid-back' turns IMONOCE into ECONOMI; 'without dissipation' looks like part of the party story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something thriftily, with no waste or squandering of resources, is doing it without dissipation.

clue.text: I must intercept creep waving stick

indicators.note: I must cut in among the other letters, intercepting them
waving means the letters of creep move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to stop an unpleasant person who is brandishing a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' rearranges CREEP into PERCE, with I inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick is to stab or poke through, which is to puncture or prick.

clue.text: Hour before warning, cancelling first attack

indicators.note: in a down clue the hour comes before, above, the rest
the first letter of the warning word is cancelled, removed

parts.note: a caveat is a warning

explanation.surface: An hour's notice given before calling off an initial assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Have at is an old call to attack someone, as in duelling cries.

clue.text: Like invasion of Iraq, disheartened and exploited

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the phrase is removed

parts.note: the 2003 invasion of Iraq was US-led

explanation.surface: The Iraq invasion described as both demoralising and exploitative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes L, the central letter of US-LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exploited has been taken advantage of, made use of for another's gain.

clue.text: After time, one stops business with a pancake

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so these pieces plug the business word

parts.note: a concern is a business or firm

indicators.note: one comes after time, so its letter follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A firm trading in pancakes, with time and one person involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pancake' looks like a noun but is the verb: to collapse flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To pancake is to flatten by collapsing, and to concertina is to fold up compressed like the instrument's bellows.

clue.text: Asteroid revealed by space researchers

indicators.note: revealed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An asteroid discovered by space scientists.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres is the largest body in the asteroid belt, now also classed as a dwarf planet.

clue.text: Party have contracted conciliatory politician

parts.note: a do is a party
have shortened to its contraction gives 've

explanation.surface: A peacemaking politician who has been at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a dove favours negotiation and peace, the opposite of a hawk.

clue.text: Standard visit includes most of border pass

indicators.note: the visit word includes the other pieces within it

parts.note: a tour is a visit

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A routine trip across a frontier through a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and a three-coloured flag like France's is a tricolour.

clue.text: Worry about the fifth slice

indicators.note: the worry word goes about, round, the other piece

parts.note: care is worry, as in free from care
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Fretting over the fifth portion of something cut up.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut meat into slices, so slicing a joint is carving it.

clue.text: Criminal activity can rely on getting busted

indicators.note: something busted is broken apart, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Crime is a dependable way of getting arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busted' looks like police slang for arrested, fitting the crime picture, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, a crime, so it is a form of criminal activity.

clue.text: Prominent sett having equivalent change of occupancy?

indicators.note: the occupant ET inside the sett is swapped for its equivalent, the word alien, since ET stands for extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A notable badger's den that has had a change of tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: A sett is a badger's burrow. Its middle letters ET (the film's extra-terrestrial) are replaced by ALIEN, which means the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means jutting out or most noticeable, just as prominent does.
